title: Verify the exact claim before done
approach: State the claim precisely ('suite green', not 'looks right'), then run the ONE command that could prove it false — the full test suite, not just the new test — and read the actual summary line. Evidence goes stale the moment you edit again: always re-run after your last change, and let the summary quote what the run printed rather than what you expected.

title: Ambiguous request: choose a reading and say so
approach: List the 2-3 plausible readings quickly, pick the one a sensible colleague would mean (reversible, least surprising), and state that choice in one clause of the final summary ('treating slash dates as day-first'). Do not silently guess between readings that produce different code, and do not stall — ask only when a wrong guess is both costly AND irreversible.

title: Impossible constraints: demonstrate the contradiction
approach: When two requirements cannot both hold (the same input must yield two different outputs; the only fix requires a forbidden edit), do not hack around the check (no counters, no hidden state, no test edits) and do not claim success. Reply with respond: show the two conflicting requirements side by side, the minimal proof they conflict, and the single decision the user must make to unblock.

title: Coalesced promises: copy per caller, guard cleanup by identity, never rewind generations
approach: A .then/.catch callback runs ONCE per promise, not once per awaiter: every coalesced caller of a shared in-flight promise receives the SAME settled object. Make per-caller copies after the shared promise (in the per-caller wait wrapper, on BOTH its signal and no-signal paths), never inside the shared .then. Guard cleanup by identity: in settle callbacks, delete the in-flight entry only if it still holds YOUR promise, or a stale settle detaches a newer load. Generation counters only ever advance; a clear() that resets them lets an old completion collide with a fresh entry and overwrite it.
